newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares slip following emerging markets.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares slip following emerging markets.

text.p: Leading Russian shares fell on Wednesday in thin morning trading reflecting the general downward trend in emerging markets, traders said.

"The market is quite weak today," said Bruswick brokerage director Martin Diggle. "It is a problem because all global emerging markets are weak at the moment. The reason is there are expectations the U.S. Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next week and this will probably be bad for emerging markets."
The U.S. Federal Open Market Committee will meet to deliberate interest rates on March 25.
Traders gave different opinions of how the market would close.
Diggle forecast prices would drift lower, but Alfa-Capital chief trader Mikhail Khaleyev said he expected prices to edge up by midday.
Norilsk Nickel ordinary and preferred shares were among loss leaders as the news about a possible share issue added to investors' worries, Khaleyev said.
Norilsk Nickel NKEL.RTS ordinary shares fell to $6.03 from $6.37 at Tuesday's close, Norilsk preferred NKEL_p.RTS shares were $4.06 after $4.70.
The company may have to make a new share issue as part of its debt restructuring plan, former First Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Potanin said on Tuesday.
Retailer GUM GUMM.RTS was one of the rare gainers with prices rising to $28.30 from $28.25.
On Tuesday Salomon Brothers said it had rated GUM a buy following the company's susstained revenues and earnings growth.
Shares in national power utility UES EESR.RTS fell to $0.2130 from $0.2225, Irkutskenergo IRGZ.RTS was $0.253 after $0.260.
